title: TODAY Halloween 2026 Recap: See the Costume Reveals and Best Moments
text:
TODAY Halloween 2026 Recap: See All The Costume Reveals and Best Moments 
 Up to 69% off Spode and More Holiday Hosting Finds Seen on TODAY 
 EVENT ENDED Last updated October 30, 2026, 2:49 PM EDT TODAY Halloween 2026 Recap: See the Costume Reveals and Best Moments
 It’s that time again, when TODAY celebrates Halloween! Relive the unforgettable costume reveals, special guests and four hours of frightfully good fun.
 See TODAY’s Costumes for the 2026 Halloween Extravaganza 15:10 
 Updated October 30, 2026, 2:49 PM EDT By Sarah Lemire and Kimmy Yam TODAY Halloween 2026: See the Best Moments 
 AN ANNUAL HALLOWEEN TRADITION: TODAY has been celebrating Halloween, with epic costume reveals on the plaza for decades.
 THEME REVEAL FOR 2026: This year, the TODAY team celebrated 100 years of NBC!
 GO BEHIND THE SCENES: See what it took to bring this annual juggernaut to life.
 FOUR HOURS OF HALLOWEEN FUN: From start to finish, it was all Halloween-themed on Friday, Oct. 30. From TODAY and 3 rd Hour of TODAY, to Jenna & Sheinelle, it was the Halloween party of the season, where they celebrated with some Halloween tips, spooky treats, costumes, surprises and oh-so-much more. 
 NEW UPDATES 3d ago / 2:49 PM EDT That's a Wrap on TODAY's Halloween Festivities 
 Another successful and fun-filled Halloween from the TODAY plaza has come and gone. 
 Have a great Happy Halloween weekend!
 3d ago / 1:15 PM EDT Go Behind the Scenes of NBC Halloween 2026 
 It's takes a dedicated team to bring TODAY's annual Halloween extravaganza to the plaza each year. See how it all comes together in this behind-the-scenes look at how Halloween 2026 came together. 
 3d ago / 1:06 PM EDT Vicky Nguyen or Alysa Liu on the Ice? You Be the Judge 
 It's not every day that you see an Olympian skating on the Rockefeller Center Skating Rink. But sure enough, we spotted Alysa Liu showing off her skills!
 Hold on a minute, that's actually Vicky Nguyen, NBC's daily news anchor and chief consumer investigative correspondent! 
 Nguyen dressed as the gold medal-winning skater for her segment this morning on TODAY and couldn't resist strutting her stuff on Rockefeller's iconic ice rink. While Nguyen didn't twizzle or complete a triple Axel, we're still so impressed with her performance. A perfect score!
 3d ago / 12:24 PM EDT The One Where Savannah Guthrie Becomes Rachel 
 To become Rachel Green from "Friends," Savannah first had to get the one and only "Rachel" haircut. 
 OK, so maybe she didn't actually go under the snippers, but the TODAY anchor did spend some time in the "SNL" wig department, getting a spot-on replica.
 Built by "SNL's" Emmy-winning wig team, Savannah's hair was totally giving us Jen Aniston vibes and inspiring us to hit "play" on the classic Rembrandts' theme song. The best part? No one was on a break. 
 3d ago / 12:21 PM EDT Simone Biles Responds to Laura Jarrett's Simone Biles Costume and You're Going to Love It 
 Emulating one of the world's most preeminent athletes is hard. So getting a compliment from the champion herself? Iconic. 
 We all can agree that three-time Olympian Simone Biles is the all-time GOAT. That's why the gymnast was top of mind when it came to choosing Laura Jarrett's Olympic costume for 2026. We were all blown away by Laura's "floor routine," which looked suspiciously like Biles gold medal-winning performance at the 2024 Summer Games. 
 Biles herself weighed in on Laura's look this year, posting two laughing emojis and two finger-pointing emojis at Laura's Halloween reveal on Instagram, and wrote in all caps: "PERFECT."
 Well done, Laura. Well done.
 3d ago / 12:12 PM EDT 'SNL' Wig Designer, Jodi Mancuso, Spills the Tea on This Year’s 'Dos 
 Though it may look effortless, bringing the TODAY Halloween show to the plaza each year is a well-coordinated symphony.
 Of course, there are the TODAY anchors and co-hosts who dress up and perform as their respective characters. But what you might not know is that each of them has a team of operatives who help create their larger-than-life looks.
 Among them is Jodi Mancuso, head hair designer for “Saturday Night Live.” Mancuso has been on the ‘SNL’ wig beat for more than 25 years and has nine Emmys to show for her incredible hair designs.
 If you think that the wigs worn by the SNL cast or the TODAY hosts come pre-made in a box, think again. Each wig is custom-made by Mancuso and her team. The time it takes to build each of the wigs, and then style them, depends on the individual wig itself and how complex it is. 
 The average wig takes around 80 hours of work, she said. But, Mancuso explained, that she and her team can construct one in roughly half the time. 
 “We can do it in 40 hours for ‘SNL’ because we don’t have 80 hours,” she said, laughing.
 “It’s quite intense,” she said. 
 It takes SNL's wig designer Jodi Mancuso and her team roughly 40 hours to create each of the TODAY hosts' Halloween wigs.   TODAY 
 TODAY 
 With that in mind, Mancuso’s crew works closely with the TODAY team to ensure everything is ready to go the morning of the Halloween show. She explained that the producers, newscaster and the costume design and makeup departments all work on their unique portions of the costumes. Then, the elements finally merge on the day of the big show. 
 “We have a lot of trust in each other,” said Mancuso of the process. “We’re all kind of in our own world, separated, styling one person and it all comes together that day.” 
 According to Mancuso, this year’s looks have been a bit easier than years past given that four of the TODAY co-hosts didn’t require wigs: Al, Willie, Laura and Sheinelle.
 Of the five who did, Mancuso said that building Craig’s Snoop Dogg hair required the most time. Carson’s Ella Langley look was also a challenge, especially in getting Langley’s distinctive color just right.
 Dylan’s “I Dream of Jeannie” hair was surprisingly tricky since, between the wig and the hat, the ‘do is heavier than it looks. 
 “It’s a lot of hair in that,” said Mancuso of the blonde, braided wig, which required the team to do some extra tweaking to make it wearable for Dylan.
 Overall, Mancuso said that helping bring the TODAY Halloween extravaganza to life each year is always a good time.
 “It’s fun. It’s for a good thing. They get excited,” said Mancuso of the TODAY anchors. “They get so excited about the people outside and showing everybody. So, it’s fun, it’s nice. We get joy out of it.”
 3d ago / 12:07 PM EDT Dylan Dreyer Reveals the Ab Workout That Helped Her Get Ready for her Epic 'I Dream of Jeannie' 
 Dylan Dreyer’s six-pack started with a piece of advice from her dad.
 For TODAY’s annual Halloween extravaganza on Oct. 30, the co-anchor transformed into Jeannie from the classic sitcom “I Dream of Jeannie,” complete with a wig, a stunning wardrobe and a midriff-baring top that put her toned midsection center stage.
 “I have always, except for when I was pregnant, had a six-pack,” Dylan tells TODAY.com. “And it’s literally because when I was younger, my dad always said to me, ‘Tighten your stomach.’”
 Marc J. Franklin for TODAY 
 So she did, and she never stopped. Keeping her core tight as she went about her day became second nature, a built-in workout decades before it ever had a national audience.
 “It’s not like I’m sitting there doing 1,000 sit-ups a day to get my stomach in shape,” she says.
 (One caveat for anyone tempted to copy her: Physical therapists warn that constantly sucking in your stomach can lead to “ hourglass syndrome ,” a pattern in which the diaphragm can’t fully expand, causing shallow breathing, back pain and extra pressure on the pelvic floor.)
 Still, Dylan didn’t leave the big reveal to chance.
 “I have stepped up my game a little bit in the last couple weeks because I knew this costume was coming,” she says.
 Her secret weapon is the Soto Method, a program created by trainer Hilary Hoffman. The name stands for “60 on, 10 on:” Each block opens with a 60-second isometric hold, followed by 10 moves meant to push the muscles to failure. Dylan’s go-to routine ends with a five-minute core finisher designed to leave the muscles burning.
 Read more about Dylan's ab workout here . 
 3d ago / 11:58 AM EDT We Caught Jenna Preparing For Her 'Smelly Cat' Performance 
 Every great performer puts in the work, and Jenna Bush Hager is no exception. 
 Our cameras caught the TODAY host, belting out her rendition of the Phoebe Buffay original, "Smelly Cat," through her dressing room door, ahead of her big performance for the show's Halloween extravaganza. 
 Jenna even put up a sign outside her "rehearsal space" that read, "DO NOT ENTER. LIVE ANIMAL." She eventually opened the door to reveal that she had been singing her heart out with her cat Maisie Moo in her arms. 
 Her commitment is *chef's kiss*. 
 3d ago / 11:46 AM EDT Watch Craig Melvin Prepare to 'Drop It Like It's Hot' 
 If you're going to channel one of music's most iconic artists, getting into character is mandatory. Ahead of his costume reveal this morning, Craig listened to the rapper's 2004 hit "Drop It Like It's Hot" while sitting in the makeup chair. 
 But that wasn't all, TODAY's anchor revealed that the song has been on repeat. 
 "I've spent the better part of the last 24 hours listening to this song over and over, so when I get out there, I can actually drop it like it's hot," he said. 
 3d ago / 11:17 AM EDT Halloween Trivia Q&A 
 Jenna and Sheinelle tested their Halloween knowledge with a fun trivia segment on Jenna & Sheinelle. If you'd like to put your own Halloween IQ to the test, see below for a roundup of Halloween trivia questions and answers. See how many you can guess!
 Rockwell’s 1984 song “Somebody’s Watching Me” features what pop singer on the chorus? Answer: Michael Jackson 
 Which character in “It’s the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown” believes in the Great Pumpkin? Answer: Linus 
 What’s the name of the vocal group that accompanies the Coffin Bangers in the song “Monster Mash”? Answer: The Crypt-Kicker Five 
 What are the names of the three Sanderson sisters in the movie “Hocus Pocus”? Answer: Winifred, Mary and Sarah 
 Which U.S. city hosts the world’s largest Halloween parade? Answer: New York City 
 Which actor played Laurie Strode in the 1978 movie “Halloween?” Answer: Jamie Lee Curtis 
 Which actor delivers the spooky monologue at the end of Michael Jackson’s “Thriller”? Answer: Vincent Price 
 Are pumpkins technically a fruit or vegetable? Answer: Fruit 
 What ancient Celtic festival is said to be the basis for modern-day Halloween? Answer: Samhain 
 Which Halloween candy was originally referred to as “chicken feed?” Answer: Candy corn 
 Keep the fun going with this comprehensive collection of Halloween trivia questions and answers . 
 3d ago / 10:58 AM EDT Carla Hall Joined for a Hall-O-Week Takeover 
 Carla Hall, chef and host of the Bravo cooking competition show "The Chew," prepared a variety of Halloween treats in honor of Oct. 31. 
 Dressed as Dwayne Wayne from the '90s sitcom "A Different World," Hall, Jenna and Sheinelle get into the spooky spirit by conjuring up Halloween-themed recipes. 
 The chef whipped up some roasted carrot ghosts and mummies in a blanket, as well as a yummy chocolate oatcake graveyard. 
 3d ago / 10:49 AM EDT Watch as Sheinelle Becomes a Radio City Rockette 
 Each and every year Sheinelle brings her A-game to TODAY's Halloween extravaganza. But 2026 is a year no one will soon forget! 
 TODAY's co-host blew everyone away when she joined the renowned Radio City Rockettes. Wearing a costume fittingly inspired by a Christmas tree, Sheinelle held her own with the legendary dancers, even performing in the signature, flawless kickline!
 TODAY 
 “I’ll be honest with you; I stopped ballet in seventh grade and The Rockettes are very much so precise and technical and ballet-adjacent," Sheinelle told TODAY.com. "So, this has been the most difficult, technically, that I’ve ever tried to attempt on the TODAY show.” 
 Reflecting on her many Halloweens with TODAY, Sheinelle said, "“I’m so darn thankful for our viewers.” 
 “I remember growing up and seeing Katie Couric swinging from the rafters as Peter Pan," she said. "So, to be a part of that legacy is not lost on me. I love that we’re still doing it and we’re still going strong and every year we have new ideas. I joke that all of us were overachievers in high school,” 
 Sheinelle added that the holiday show is "our chance as adults to lean in and have a great time.”
 Watch Sheinelle practice with the famous dance troupe ahead of today's reveal.
 3d ago / 10:42 AM EDT Jenna & Sheinelle Inspired Halloween Costumes? Yes, Please! 
 The team outdid themselves this year by creating a variety of costumes, inspired by memorable moments and elements from the show. See below for some of their best looks.
 Remember when Leslie Jones picked up Sheinelle Jones? We do! This legendary moment is captured in the costume below.
 Marc J. Franklin for TODAY 
 Next up is the pink chair from Jenna & Sheinelle. Who knew it could translate into the perfect costume?
 Marc J. Franklin for TODAY 
 Who can forget Jenna's award-winning basket of cucumbers? Her garden-grown cukes make for a totally fresh look!
 Marc J. Franklin for TODAY 
 Of course, there was the pair's trip to the "Purlates" studio, where Jenna enjoyed doing pilates with cats and Sheinelle, well, she went along with it, even though she was terrified. The Halloween costume below is one of the Purlates cats, ready to workout. 
 Marc J. Franklin for TODAY 
 Finally, it's Jenna and Sheinelle dressed up as their iconic theme song. Okay, it's not really the co-hosts, but, holy costumes, they sure look like it!
 Marc J. Franklin for TODAY 
 3d ago / 10:15 AM EDT Jenna Performed an Ode to "Sheinelley Cat" 
 Jenna reprised her role as Phoebe Buffay from "Friends" to kick off Jenna & Sheinelle. 
 With a guitar in hand, Jenna rewrote the classic tune "Smelly Cat" to pay tribute to her daytime TV partner and all the "coffee and kitty-lovers out there." If you missed it, here are the new (and improved) lyrics to "Smelly Cat, oops, we mean "Sheinelley Cat."
 TODAY 
 "Sheinelley Cat, Sheinelley Cat, I love Halloween with you. Sheinelley Cat, Sheinelley Cat, you give it your all. They don't let me ever dance, they don't want to take the chance. Sheinelley Cat, Sheinelley Cat, kick high, but do not fall."
 3d ago / 9:55 AM EDT Get Into the Spirit of the Season With These Spooky Cocktails 
 Tim Sweeney, the beverage director at Pebble Bar, joined the 3rd Hour of TODAY to mix up a batch of spooky cocktails. It's Halloween after all and there's no better way to celebrate than with a few on-theme beverages.
 For his costume, Sweeney paid tribute to his hometown baseball team and 2026 World Series champs, the Milwaukee Brewers! 
 Sweeney whipped up a variety of delectable drinks including the "Devil's Margarita," "Peach Ring Candy Cocktail" and the "Corpse Reviver No. 2," what he called the sure cure for a hangover. 
 3d ago / 9:49 AM EDT Chloe Melas Is ... Count Dracula 
 Chloe Melas, NBC's entertainment correspondent, joins in the spooky fun this morning dressed as the very scary Count Dracula.
 TODAY 
 "I'm rowing myself into the segment right now," Melas joked ahead of her story on The Great Pumpkin Regatta, the annual water race carried out all over the country.
 Instead of boats, participants row enormous hollowed out pumpkins. 
 Find out more about this unusual activity below. 
 3d ago / 9:43 AM EDT Vicky Nguyen Is ... Alysa Liu 
 Vicky Nguyen is gliding right into Halloween. 
 With a head of iconic halo hair, the NBC News chief consumer investigative correspondent is none other than Olympic champion ice skater Alysa Liu. 
 Liu initially announced her retirement from figure skating in 2022, walking away from the sport after her Olympic debut in Beijing. But she reemerged in headlines for her triumphant return to the sport in 2026, when she took home two gold medals at the Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics. 
 Vicky told TODAY.com that she had the opportunity to meet the Olympian, who she described as an “incredible role model.” She said that she’s excited to bring Liu’s look to life. 
 Courtesy Vicky Nguyen 
 “I actually got to meet Alisa when she was here for the Today Show after she won her gold medal,” Vicky said. “She could not have been more joyous, bubbly, kind — just a beautiful pixie who represents to me what we hope for in sports, which is someone who does it for the love of the sport, does it with so much happiness and all of their training and dedication pays off in this incredible way.”
 There’s also another plus. 
 Marc J. Franklin for TODAY 
 “We’re about the same height,” Vicky said. “I just think it’ll be a fun tribute costume.” 
 With figure skating being so central to Liu’s identity, we had to ask: Can Vicky skate? 
 “I certainly cannot do a jump or an axle or anything like that, but I can get around the rink. My daughters are impressed with my skating abilities,” she said. “I can do a few swizzles and twizzles and twirls. But thankfully I won’t be having to ice skate here.” 
 3d ago / 9:28 AM EDT Jack McBrayer Joins to Talk ’30 Rock’ and 'Zillow Gone Wild!' 
 After his surprise appearance during this morning’s big costume reveal, Jack McBrayer, aka Kenneth the eternally cheerful NBC page, returned to recap this morning's inspired “30 Rock” performance and talk about the show’s recent reunion. It’s hard to believe, but the Tina Fey comedy is marking its 20th anniversary!
 According to the actor and comedian, he still has his page outfit and even loaned it out to his friend, Emmy winner Alexander Skarsgard, for Halloween one year!
 TODAY 
 McBrayer also talked about his latest series “Zillow Gone Wild.” The HGTV show features some of the country’s most eccentric real estate listings. 
 Fun fact: McBrayer is good at remembering birthdays and always calls his friends on their special day. Among them? Henry Winkler, Conan O'Brien and, of course, his long-time besties from "30 Rock."
 3d ago / 9:26 AM EDT Halloween By The Numbers 
 We love Halloween and the numbers prove it. 
 This year, an estimated 96% of consumers are expected to buy sweets for the spooky occasion, shelling out $4.1 billion on candy alone, according to the National Retail Federation. More than three-quarters are expected to buy decorations. 
 Check out more fascinating statistics about the annual night of tricks and treats. 
 Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups are the top selling candy on Instacart, across most of America, representing the No. 1 candy in 40 of the 50 states and D.C. Sour Patch Kids reign supreme in Rhode Island, the only state where the sour candy overtook both the Peanut Butter Cups and Peanut M&M’s, according to data from the platform. 
 The Pacific Northwest seems to have a sweet tooth! The top five candy-buying cities on Instacart are in Oregon, Washington and Alaska. Those in the northeast buy the least amount of candy.
 To the dismay of children everywhere, about 79% of parents say they take Halloween candy from their kids, according to 2020 data from the National Confectioners Association. 
 The top trending kids’ costume on Google this year is none other than the Queen of Country, Dolly Parton. 
 An estimated 4.6 million children are planning to dress up as Spider-Man this year, according to the National Retail Federation. 
 3d ago / 9:19 AM EDT Jenna's Cat Maisie Is Purrfect as 'Smelly Cat' 
 Jenna Bush Hager might just have the most chill feline on the planet. 
 Joining the rest of the team in TODAY's Halloween reveal is Maisie Moo Bush Hager, Jenna's real-life cat. 
 The very mellow Maisie made a guest appearance as the iconic "Smelly Cat" from the hit sitcom "Friends."
 Savannah, Jenna and Maisie Moo Bush Hager.   Marc J. Franklin for TODAY 
 The adorable kitty recently joined the duo on Jenna & Sheinelle . 
 “She’s a beautiful cat,” Sheinelle said, who admits she's not a cat person — but she might just be one after meeting Maisie.
 “She’s kind of puppy-like. Is that offensive to cat people?” she wondered.
 Maisie wandering Studio 1A.   TODAY 
 3d ago / 9:18 AM EDT Brian Cheung Is ... George Washington 
 Brian Cheung's Halloween costume is revolutionary. Literally! 
 The NBC business and data correspondent is giving us total presidential vibes dressed as the OG founding father, George Washington. 
 Cheung joins the 3rd Hour of TODAY to deliver some interesting statistics on everyone's favorite spooky holiday. 
 TODAY 
 3d ago / 9:06 AM EDT The TODAY Team Return to the Plaza: Here's a Recap of Their Fabulous 2026 Costumes! 
 Marc J. Franklin for TODAY 
 Willie Geist Is … Johnny Carson
 Savannah Guthrie is … Rachel Green from “Friends”
 Jenna Bush Hager is … Phoebe Buffay from “Friends”
 Al Roker Is … Gumby From ‘Saturday Night Live’
 Carson Daly Is … Ella Langley
 Dylan Dreyer Is … Jeannie From "I Dream of Jeannie"
 Laura Jarrett Is … Simone Biles
 Craig Melvin Is … Snoop Dogg
 Sheinelle Jones Is … A Radio City Rockette
 Maisie (Jenna's cat) Is ... Smelly Cat
 3d ago / 8:52 AM EDT Costume Designer Staci Greenbaum Takes Us Behind the Scenes of Halloween 2026 
 TODAY has been putting on a legendary Halloween show for decades! And in recent years, many of the costumes have been from the mind of costume designer Staci Greenbaum.
 Greenbaum, who began collaborating with the TODAY team in 2023 when the theme was “Kellyoke,” says she loves being a part of TODAY’s costume extravaganza.
 “Every year is something different, but this year’s been really fun,” Greenbaum told TODAY.com in a sit-down interview earlier this week. 
 The occasion isn’t without its unique challenges, according to the costume designer, who started with creating Savannah and Jenna’s “Friends” looks.
 Given that the sitcom aired for 10 seasons, Greenbaum says it was tricky, pinning down a single iconic look for characters Rachel and Phoebe. Instead, she took inspiration from a variety of looks over the years.
 Savannah Wetzel (left) and Staci Greenbaum (right) spent countless hours creating this year's Halloween costumes for TODAY.   Marc J. Franklin for TODAY 
 “We’re taking some liberties,” she explained of the costumes, which are more about capturing the essence of the characters, rather than duplicating specific outfits worn by cast members Jennifer Aniston and Lisa Kudrow.
 Along with the “Friends” looks, Greenbaum said that other costumes this year, including Craig’s Snoop Dogg, Laura’s Simone Biles and Willie’s Johnny Carson, were more nods than they were real-life replications.
 “We’re talking about costumes that span a range of different things that encapsulate NBC’s centennial. So, some of them have very direct inspiration and some of them don’t,” explained Greenbaum.
 There was definitely some accurate cosplay among the costumes, too. Al’s Gumby costume, for example, was a real-life replica of Eddie Murphy’s ‘SNL’ character and Carson’s Ella Langley look was reproduced from her hit video for “Choosin’ Texas.” Dylan’s Jeannie costume was also a duplicate, mirroring Barbara Eden’s iconic maroon-and-pink genie outfit from the ‘60s show.
 Of all the costumes this year, Sheinelle’s was likely the most inspired, Greenbaum explained. Rather than having Sheinelle dress up in the exact Rockettes costume, the designer said she took a cue from a joke Sheinelle made about wanting to be a tree for Halloween this year. 
 “I said, ‘Well, during Christmas, we have the tree lighting.’ So, her costume is more reminiscent of the Rockefeller Tree. It’s green, gold, red and silver and it has the same fringe and movement (of The Rockettes’ costume), but I’m making her what she asked for,” laughed Greenbaum. 
 Read on for other notable details from this year’s costumes:
 Laura’s one-piece costume was made by the same manufacturer that creates the real Olympic leotards for Team USA.
 Carson’s red halter top and suede chaps were custom-made by the costume team.
 Savannah’s page outfit is a real NBC page uniform, borrowed from the program.
 Al’s Gumby was made by the same “SNL” team that built the costume for Eddie Murphy’s return to Weekend Update in 2019.
 3d ago / 8:51 AM EDT Witches Brew, Ghastly Goulash and Spiderweb Cheesecake, Oh My! 
 What’s Halloween without a few spooky beverages and snacks to take the celebration to the next level? Back from her segment with “Snoop Dogg” is the queen of Halloween: Martha Stewart. 
 Stewart joined Savannah, Craig and Carson to cook up some hauntingly delicious dishes in honor of Oct. 31. The media mogul and lifestyle expert kicked things off with some spooky apple "shrunken heads." The clever creations were the perfect addition for bourbon cider punch. 
 For the main course, Stewart whipped up a batch of ghostly goulash served in a hollowed out pumpkin.
 Dessert was a spiderweb cheesecake sure to impress friends and family alike. While making her no-bake dessert, Craig had a total mishap, spilling some of the chocolate on Stewart's white tracksuit. 
 "Real Snoop would never do that!" chastised Stewart.
 3d ago / 8:40 AM EDT NBC Trivia and Fun Facts 
 TODAY 
 Jack McBrayer, aka Kenneth Parcell from "30 Rock," joins the TODAY team in a fun game of NBC trivia. 
 In honor of NBC’s big birthday, check out the list below for fun facts and trivia all about the Peacock network.
 NBC officially launched on Nov. 15, 1926.
 NBC stands for the National Broadcasting Company.
 NBC is the oldest major broadcast network in the U.S.
 NBC began as a radio network.
 NBC station WNBT aired television’s first commercial on July 1, 1941.
 Meet the Press debuted as a radio program in 1945.
 NBC launched its first regularly scheduled newscast in 1949.
 The TODAY show launched on Jan. 14, 1952.
 The first Tonight Show aired on Sept. 27, 1954, with host Steve Allen.
 Richard Nixon and John F. Kennedy participated in the first televised presidential debate on NBC in 1960.
 Johnny Carson took over as host of The Tonight Show on Oct. 1, 1962.
 The summer Olympic games in Tokyo were aired on NBC in 1964.
 In 1967, NBC broadcasted the first Super Bowl.
 Saturday Night Live debuted on Oct. 11, 1975
 “The Golden Girls” premiered on NBC in 1985 and ran for 7 seasons.
 In 1998, the Emmy-winning series “Seinfeld” debuted.
 “Law & Order” aired its first episode in 1990.
 Iconic TV shows “ER” and “Friends” launched on NBC in 1994.
 Telemundo and Bravo joined the NBC family in 2002.
 The Emmy-winning series “The Office” debuted in 2005.
 Sunday Night Football officially returned to NBC in 2006.
 Seth Meyers and Jimmy Fallon officially became late-night talk show hosts in the same year — 2014.
 Telemundo broadcasted its first FIFI World Cup in 2018
 In 2020, NBC’s streaming service Peacock launched.
 NBC Nightly News celebrated 75 years in 2023.
 In 2026, NBC marks 100 years!
 3d ago / 8:31 AM EDT What Is The NBC Page Program? 
 If you’ve ever watched sitcom “30 Rock,” then you’re probably familiar with Kenneth Parcell, the cheerful page with the can-do attitude, played by Jack McBrayer. The role is based on NBC’s real-life page program, which was launched in 1933 with the aim of fostering the careers of promising young professionals. 
 Indeed, many recognizable names have gotten their start in the page program, including Gregory Peck, Aubrey Plaza, Regis Philbin, Willard Scott, Ted Koppel and Michael Eisner, just to name a few! 
 The illustrious page program lasts anywhere from 12 to 16 months and draws thousands of applicants each year. Of them, less than 2% – or roughly 200 people a year – are accepted, making it one of the most coveted posts in media.
 3d ago / 8:22 AM EDT Surprise! It's Jack McBrayer From '30 Rock' 
 In another inspired cameo, it's Jack McBrayer, better known as Kenneth Parcell, from "30 Rock." The always-happy and eternally young NBC page joins Savannah at the end of today's NBC tour!
 Marc J. Franklin for TODAY 
 Airing from 2006 to 2013, Tina Fey’s iconic sendup of the behind-the-scenes shenanigans of a sketch comedy show is one of NBC’s most enduring sitcoms. Also starring Alec Baldwin, Tracy Morgan and Jane Krakowski, the long-running show scored 16 Primetime Emmys and remains a comedy staple in syndication. 
 "That was quite the tour!" said "Kenneth" approvingly, before giving Savannah her official NBC page pin and saying she should be "proud as a peacock to wear it."
 Fun fact: The rest of the crowd joining Savannah and McBrayer on the TODAY stage are real NBC pages.
 3d ago / 8:21 AM EDT Sheinelle Jones Is ... A Radio City Rockette 
 Through the years, Sheinelle has channeled a variety of legendary performers for TODAY’s Halloween show including Tina Turner, Beyoncé, Bruno Mars and Janet Jackson. Now, the co-host of “Jenna & Sheinelle” pays tribute to an NBC Rockefeller Center staple — The Radio City Rockettes!
 The renowned dance troupe has been performing for more than 100 years and is a big part of NBC’s storied history. Whether it’s at the Rockefeller Center Tree Lighting or the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, the Rockettes have been on hand to mark some of the biggest events of the last century.
 Sheinelle joins the dance troupe on the plaza to once again prove that when it comes to dance moves, she’s totally got the chops! According to Sheinelle, learning to dance alongside The Rockettes was no small feat.
 “I think that so many people underestimate the athletic and dance abilities of The Rockettes,” Sheinelle told TODAY.com in a sit-down interview the week before the reveal.
 Marc J. Franklin for TODAY 
 “We see them as these beautiful ladies. They’re showgirls. They have high kicks,” Sheinelle said. “Let me tell you something — these women are incredible and I am learning that in real time.”
 To prepare for this year’s performance, Sheinelle rehearsed with The Rockettes and said that while she’s danced in prior Halloween reveals, this year’s routine is truly next-level.
 “I’ll be honest with you; I stopped ballet in seventh grade and The Rockettes are very much so precise and technical and ballet-adjacent. So, this has been the most difficult, technically, that I’ve ever tried to attempt on the TODAY show,” Sheinelle said.
 “It looks easier than it is and I think that’s the magic of The Rockettes — they make it look so easy, but technically it is very difficult. So,” she said. “I am really having to work hard.”
 Sheinelle added that when it comes to this year’s Halloween reveal, she’s got one mission: “My hope and my goal is to make my seventh-grade self proud.”
 Sheinelle said that like many women, she grew up watching the famed dance troupe and envisioned what it would be like to join their elite ranks.
 “So, I feel like I’m representing the average woman who’s like, ‘I’ve got a little bit of dance in me, what if we went on a wild adventure and joined the Radio City Music Hall Rockettes?’”
 3d ago / 8:19 AM EDT Surprise! It's Martha Stewart! 
 Look who it is! It’s Snoop’s bestie Martha Stewart! Joining Craig is the real-life Stewart. Without a doubt, she’s 100% the gin to “Snoop’s” juice.
